articles.title: Indian students in US decline 6%, Chinese numbers fall 4% as American campuses face deeper enrolment crisis
articles.summary: MUMBAI: For years, the United States was the destination of choice for Indian students looking for a foreign degree and, perhaps, a career to follow.
articles.body: MUMBAI: For years, the United States was the destination of choice for Indian students looking for a foreign degree and, perhaps, a career to follow. That promise is beginning to look less certain. Indian student numbers in American universities fell 6% to 3,39,435 in 2025-26, while those from China declined 4% to 2,54,458, as visa uncertainties, a difficult employment market and shifting immigration policies complicate decisions about studying in the US.The more revealing figure is the number of students entering American institutions for the first time. New international enrolments fell 18% to 2,28,123 in 2025-26. Unlike total student numbers, which include those admitted in earlier years, fresh enrolments provide a clearer indication of whether students are still choosing the US.And the Fall 2026 Snapshot suggests the weakness will continue. Participating institutions reported a 15% fall in graduate students, a 3% decline in undergraduates and a 6% drop in OPT numbers. New international enrolments were down 15% compared with the previous fall.The decline is part of a wider retreat. International student numbers across American higher education institutions fell 3% to 11,46,163 in 2025-26, according to the Open Doors 2026 report released on Nov 16 by the Institute of International Education (IIE). And the slide may not be over. A separate Fall 2026 Snapshot survey of more than 800 institutions has recorded a sharper 9% fall in international student numbers in the ongoing academic year, with new enrolments dropping 15%.From record highs to a sharp retreat: The India storyFor India, the reversal is particularly striking. Just a year earlier, in 2024-25, the country had sent a record 3,63,019 students to the US, a 10% increase over the previous year. India remains the largest source of international students for the third consecutive year, ahead of China, but the momentum that carried it to the top appears to have weakened. Together, the two countries still account for nearly 52% of all international students in the US.The steepest fall has come at the graduate level, traditionally the strongest draw for Indian students, particularly those pursuing engineering, technology and management programmes. Indian graduate student numbers plunged 34% to 1,16,609, while undergraduate enrolments slipped just 1% to 39,711.The distinction is telling. For many Indian families, a master's degree in the US is not merely an academic investment. It is also a route to professional experience, better earnings and, potentially, a longer-term career abroad. That calculation becomes harder when the cost of an American education remains high but the prospects of securing a job afterwards are uncertain.The overall fall in Indian student numbers would have been much sharper had it not been for those already working in the US, said study-abroad. The number of Indians on OPT rose 27% to 1,82,201, accounting for more than half of all Indian students counted in the report.China, meanwhile, also recorded a more moderate decline. Its graduate student population fell 5% to 1,14,043, undergraduate numbers dropped 5% to 74,594, and OPT participation declined 1% to 61,545.Across nationalities, graduate enrolments fell 13% to 4,23,078, largely because of a 22% contraction in master's students. Doctoral numbers, however, rose 3%, while undergraduate enrolments were virtually unchanged at 3,56,165.American campuses feel the pinchThe OPT figures are particularly noteworthy. In 2025-26, participation had risen 14% to 3,35,785, supported by the large number of international students who had graduated in previous years. The latest survey suggests that even this segment, which had helped cushion the overall decline, is beginning to contract.For American universities, the implications extend beyond admissions. International students are an important source of tuition revenue, research talent and skilled graduates. According to the US Department of Commerce, they contributed nearly $56 billion to the American economy in 2025.Yet the appetite for recruiting them remains strong. In the Fall Snapshot, 75% of institutions cited the value of international perspectives on campus, while 60% acknowledged the financial contributions of international students. As many as 91% said recruiting international students in science, technology, engineering and mathematics remained a priority.Computer science was identified as a recruitment priority by 75% of institutions, followed by engineering and biological sciences at 59% each. In 2025-26, STEM disciplines accounted for 57% of international students, with mathematics and computer science drawing 2,86,168 students and engineering another 2,14,193.Some countries buck the downtrendNot every country, however, has seen its numbers fall. Nine of the 25 largest source countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Vietnam and Italy, reported record-high student populations. The divergent trends suggest that the slowdown is not uniform and that the international student landscape is changing in ways that cannot be explained by a single factor.Jason Czyz, president and CEO of IIE, said international education continued to strengthen American institutions and foster relationships that extended beyond students' time on campus.The report also recorded a 5% increase in American students studying abroad for academic credit, with 3,13,824 doing so in 2024-25. articles.title: Epstein's death may not have been suicide, new analysis suggests
articles.summary: Forensics expert Dr. Michael Freeman says multiple images and overlooked details about Jeffrey Epstein's death contradict the conclusion that he died by suic...
articles.body:
Warning: This article and video contain graphic images that may be disturbing.

Across the political spectrum, a large chunk of Americans believe, despite a lack of evidence, that Jeffrey Epstein did not die by suicide.

Now one forensics expert, working with photos and files provided by Epstein's brother, is weighing in to contend that this suspicion might be right.

Dr. Michael Freeman , who is editor-in-chief of the Journal of Forensic and Legal Medicine, spent months reviewing never-before-published autopsy records provided to him and CBS News by Epstein's brother. The 2019 ruling by the New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner was that Epstein died by suicide. But Freeman has concluded that Epstein's death was more likely a homicide.

Freeman — who worked with Anders Eriksson, a professor of forensic medicine at Umea University in Sweden, and Itiel Dror, a researcher specializing in identifying bias in forensic decision making — presented their findings Monday in London. Freeman said he believes that in August 2019 the world's most notorious sex abuser was likely attacked and killed by another person.

"The injuries that were documented by the medical examiner were not consistent with the suicidal hanging. And the injuries that were attributed to something other than potentially a physical struggle or assault were just overlooked," Freeman told CBS News, based on his review of the autopsy records, photos and a biomedical reconstruction he produced.

The report is the second by an outside forensic expert to question the official findings of suicide. In 2020, Epstein's brother hired forensic pathologist Dr. Michael Baden to look into the death, as first reported by "60 Minutes." At the time, Baden said injuries to Epstein's neck raised doubts about the official ruling. He told "60 Minutes" the evidence he saw pointed more to murder than suicide.

Freeman's report was rejected for publication from an academic journal, he acknowledged. He said reviewers for the journal thought it wasn't appropriate to criticize a medical examiner's findings in a peer-reviewed publication. Freeman plans to resubmit, he said.

Freeman, a professor of forensic medicine, said he was struck by the first image he examined, depicting the right side of Epstein's upper body and face, with ligature wounds visible on his neck.

"When I saw this photograph, my first reaction was that that is a very unusual looking injury for a hanging on the neck," Freeman said.

Freeman has testified as a forensic expert in high-profile court cases and was a member of the Maryland attorney general's audit team that reviewed dozens of in-custody deaths last year. Still, forensic pathology is not an exact science. Credible experts often interpret the same evidence very differently. Neck injuries from hanging or strangulation can be especially ambiguous. And Epstein's death investigation was marked by added uncertainty because of a cascade of blunders in the hours, days and weeks after his body was discovered in his Manhattan federal jail cell .

The New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner — which conducted the autopsy on Aug. 11, 2019, the day after Epstein was found dead — declined an interview request, and did not reply directly to Freeman's findings when pressed by CBS News.

"Our office stands by its determination," a spokesperson for the medical examiner said.

There has been support for that finding. In June, The New York Times conducted an investigation that it said relied on tens of thousands of pages of newly released documents, as well as Epstein's own notes handwritten in jail. That report said there were indications Epstein was intent on ending his own life. And the newspaper reported that, of the forensics experts they interviewed, "almost none of them believed that his manner of death — suicide or homicide — could be conclusively settled based on the medical evidence alone."

Freeman believes the official investigation missed key details.

"The injury pattern was described as a sloped or as a peaked injury that was a perfect description for a hanging. But that's not what we saw when we saw the photos," Freeman said.

While one mark fit that description, he noticed a second mark in the ligature wounds on Epstein's neck, beneath and angled differently than the mark above it.

"There is no mechanism to produce a second mark that would be lower. Even if the ligature was tied with two loops, both loops would go up to the point where it was tied because that's the anchor point," Freeman said.

Asked if the two markings, present on each side of Epstein's neck, could have been indicative of him stopping and starting — trying twice to kill himself — Freeman said available research into suicidal hanging indicates that's unlikely. Epstein would have had to make "a false start that was strong enough to break his hyoid bone and thyroid cartilage and give him a deep abrasion and then maintain consciousness," Freeman said.

It's an explanation that doesn't make sense, he said.

"That's not what suicidal hangings do," Freeman said. "The body becomes unconscious and then it is the weight of the body that produces the abrasion, not any kind of running jump at it. That opportunity really isn't there. That's not a realistic scenario for any hanging described in any of the literature throughout the world."

None of the prison guards on duty when Epstein died spoke to medical examiner investigators, according to Justice Department records. Some of them falsified records and lied about their activities the night before and morning of Epstein's death. Corrections officer Michael Thomas is credited with finding Epstein's body. He only agreed to be interviewed by investigators after he was charged with crimes two years later.

There's no indication that the medical examiner's office revisited its determination after Thomas agreed to share his account. Freeman, however, based his reconstruction of the scene of Epstein's death on Thomas' later description, in which he said he found Epstein hanging from a bedpost.

Freeman constructed a biomechanical analysis, or series of three-dimensional models, based on Thomas' description of the scene, as well as wounds and abrasions visible in images of Epstein's body.

"The biomechanical analysis was designed to be able to map the injuries on a model that was…as close to the anatomy and size and shape of Epstein as possible," Freeman said.

The 3-D model allowed Freeman to test the suicide hypothesis. What the model showed is that some of the abrasions and injuries visible on Epstein's neck were indicative of suicidal hanging, but some on his neck, and elsewhere on his body including an injury to his shoulder, weren't.

"We have too many other injuries that are not explained by any suicidal hanging. Because I don't care how this guy is found, where did these other injuries come from?" Freeman asked. "How do you get the deep soft tissue hemorrhage in his left shoulder? How do you get the injury on his back?"

His conclusion will add fuel to the fire of conspiracy theories that have consumed much of the popular discourse around Epstein's death.

"The alternative scenario is that there was a strangulation that occurred," Freeman said. In particular, horizontal marks on Epstein's neck point to ligature being pulled from behind him, he said.

Epstein's cell was littered with piles of torn orange fabric, the bedding used in cells at the Manhattan Correctional Center. Freeman says an image shows one knotted fabric that he believes appears to support the strangulation theory.

"That is a double knotted, looped, narrow ligature that was found in the cell that was dropped in a corner near the desk. And if we put those together in a format in which the knot, one of these knots, is applied as pressure to produce this irregular abrasion at the back of the neck, we actually have a fairly good explanation for all the injuries," Freeman said.

He also noticed what he claims are signs of an assault and struggle, including blunt force trauma to the face and the left shoulder.

"And we see what appeared to be consistent with fingernail marks above the ligature," Freeman said. "And if you put it all together, it is most consistent with a homicidal strangulation from behind using a narrow knotted fabric ligature."

The fabric Freeman believes matches Epstein's injuries wasn't collected for the medical examiner.

"What you see in this front view of the ligature pattern is that it is ragged looking," Freeman said, referring to the markings on Epstein's neck. "It is segmented looking. It's not smooth. This certainly would not be consistent with the noose that was taken from the room."

Epstein's death drew global headlines and promises from the top levels of the Justice Department that it would be among the most scrutinized inmate deaths in history. Instead, it was marked by a series of failures.

The issues with Epstein's death scene began almost immediately on Aug. 10, 2019.

Thomas reported finding Epstein's body, cold to the touch, around 6:30 a.m.

"The fact that to touch, Epstein's body was cold, would indicate he had been dead for at least a few hours," Freeman said.

Epstein's body was moved out of the cell within minutes of being discovered, preventing accurate photography of the scene when investigators first arrived that day. The cell was never sealed off for forensic investigation, and much of the evidence at the scene wasn't properly preserved, a 2025 CBS News investigation found.

To make matters worse, most of the closed-circuit cameras in Epstein's wing of the prison were not functioning. And Justice Department documents show investigators who reviewed footage from the nearest working camera — one that looked over a common area connecting multiple tiers of cells — did not follow up on some details, including an unexplained orange blur seen ascending a staircase toward Epstein's block the night of his death.

It took two years for federal investigators to interview Thomas, who had been charged with lying and falsifying prison records, and provided a statement in exchange for leniency. It took another year for those same investigators to talk to the medical examiner who examined Epstein's body.

And Freeman said the medical examiner may have misinterpreted key details on Epstein's body. She noted that there were no broken fingernails or defensive wounds on the hands. An abrasion on Epstein's arm was probably from convulsing during hanging, the medical examiner said.

"When she talks about the fact that there's only a little scratch on the arm, she completely overlooks the fact that there was deep intramuscular hemorrhage in the left shoulder that was undoubtedly due to blunt force trauma," Freeman said.

To Freeman, the mystery of Epstein's death is not how he died, but who killed him.

"I'm comfortable saying that's a mystery. Who did it? Exactly how they did it. What happened? All the other things. Why the cameras [were] off? All a mystery, yes," Freeman said. "Was this a suicide? Not a mystery."

articles.title: Agenda Ribeirão traz Rafaella Tuma para falar de negócios no Sesi | G1
articles.standfirst: Encontro acontece no dia 25 de novembro, no Teatro do Sesi, em Ribeirão Preto (SP), e aborda geração de renda, qualificação profissional e oportunidades de negócios. Entrada é gratuita.
articles.summary: O Agenda Ribeirão promove debates gratuitos sobre empreendedorismo e mercado de trabalho com a presença da influenciadora Rafaella Tuma no Teatro do Sesi.
articles.body:
Quem busca oportunidades para empreender, desenvolver um negócio ou se preparar para o mercado de trabalho pode participar do Agenda Ribeirão – Empreendedorismo e Empregabilidade. O evento acontece na quarta-feira (25), em Ribeirão Preto (SP), no Teatro do Sesi. A entrada é gratuita mediante reserva de ingresso on-line .

Entre os convidados estão a ilustradora, cartunista e criadora de conteúdo Rafaella Tuma, que reúne cerca de 8 milhões de seguidores nas redes sociais.

O encontro também reúne representantes do poder público, do Serviço Brasileiro de Apoio às Micro e Pequenas Empresas (Sebrae), do Serviço Nacional de Aprendizagem Industrial (Senai) e do Serviço Social da Indústria (Sesi). A realização é da EPTV.

A ilustradora, cartunista e criadora de conteúdo Rafaella Tuma — Foto: Divulgação

Entre os assuntos que serão abordados estão as oportunidades de geração de renda, as políticas públicas de desenvolvimento econômico em Ribeirão Preto, o comportamento empreendedor e a importância da qualificação profissional para a inserção no mercado de trabalho.

Criatividade como ferramenta de negócios

Conhecida pelas animações bem-humoradas que retratam situações do cotidiano, a ribeirão-pretana Rafaella Tuma apresenta a palestra "Como Empreender com Criatividade", em parceria com o Sebrae.

A partir da própria experiência como criadora de conteúdo e empreendedora, Rafaella vai abordar como o humor, a criatividade e a presença digital podem ajudar empreendedores a divulgar produtos e serviços, aproximar marcas dos consumidores e impulsionar as vendas.

18h30 – Recepção, credenciamento e café de boas-vindas.

19h15 – Empreendedorismo e oportunidades: apresentação com Jean Vicente, secretário municipal de Governo de Ribeirão Preto, sobre o cenário do empreendedorismo na cidade, oportunidades para os jovens, geração de renda e políticas públicas de desenvolvimento econômico.

19h45 – Painel "Empreendedorismo e empregabilidade – caminhos para novas oportunidades": debate sobre qualificação profissional, comportamento empreendedor e preparação para o mercado de trabalho com Paulo Arruda, gerente regional do Sebrae; Reginaldo Dias de Souza, diretor do Senai Ribeirão Preto; e Ricardo Machado, diretor do Sesi Ribeirão Preto.

20h30 – Palestra "Como Empreender com Criatividade": com a ilustradora e criadora de conteúdo Rafaella Tuma.

Agenda Ribeirão – Empreendedorismo e Empregabilidade

Data e horário: quarta-feira (25), a partir das 18h30

Local: Teatro do Sesi – Rua João Ignacchitti, Jardim Castelo Branco, Ribeirão Preto

Vídeos: Tudo sobre Ribeirão Preto, Franca e região

articles.title: PCs gamers e grandes ofertas marcam a Black Friday da Topdek | G1
articles.standfirst: Campanha acontece de 19 a 21 de novembro, com descontos de até 70% em produtos selecionados, promoções relâmpago e sorteio de dois setups gamers completos.
articles.summary: Campanha acontece de 19 a 21 de novembro, com descontos de até 70% em produtos selecionados, promoções relâmpago e sorteio de dois setups gamers completos.
articles.body:
A Black Friday da Topdek Informática promete movimentar Ciudad del Este entre os dias 19 e 21 de novembro. Durante os três dias de campanha, os consumidores poderão encontrar descontos de até 70% em produtos selecionados, além de promoções relâmpago que poderão aparecer a qualquer momento.

Entre os destaques estão produtos procurados por quem acompanha as novidades de tecnologia, como placas de vídeo, produtos da Razer, equipamentos Apple e impressoras 3D. A seleção também inclui patinetes, motos elétricas, robôs aspiradores e outras categorias de eletrônicos.

Para o público interessado em jogos e computadores de alto desempenho, a campanha também será uma oportunidade de conhecer opções de componentes e equipamentos para montar ou atualizar um PC gamer.

Dois setups gamers completos serão sorteados

Um dos destaques da programação será o sorteio de dois setups gamers completos, marcado para sábado, dia 21 de novembro. A premiação é voltada especialmente aos entusiastas de tecnologia e jogos e promete ser um dos momentos mais aguardados da campanha.

Os visitantes também poderão participar de brincadeiras, desafios e atividades interativas, incluindo uma roleta de premiações. A dinâmica contará com diferentes possibilidades de brindes e surpresas.

Durante os três dias, haverá ainda distribuição de cupons para participação nos sorteios, conforme os horários indicados nos bilhetes. A programação também contará com pipoca para degustação dos visitantes.

A Topdek prepara uma edição especial de Black Friday para receber o público interessado em tecnologia e informática. Durante os dias de campanha, a loja terá ofertas em diferentes categorias, com oportunidades para quem procura desde componentes para computadores até equipamentos eletrônicos.

Quem visitar o estabelecimento também poderá acompanhar as promoções relâmpago e participar das atividades preparadas para a ocasião. A programação acontece no Shopping Lai Lai Center, em Ciudad del Este. Mais informações e novidades podem ser acompanhadas pelo Instagram @topdekinformatica e pelo site topdekinformatica.com.br .

articles.title: A Última Sessão de Freud em Volta Redonda: Ingressos e Datas | G1
articles.standfirst: Espetáculo será realizado no dia 25 de novembro; entrada será mediante doação de um litro de leite.
articles.summary: Espetáculo será realizado no dia 25 de novembro; entrada será mediante doação de um litro de leite.
articles.body:
Peça “A Última Sessão de Freud” com Odilon Wagner e Marcello Airoldi será apresentada em Volta Redonda — Foto: Foto divulgação - Secom/PMVR

O município de Volta Redonda (RJ) vai receber o espetáculo “A Última Sessão de Freud”, estrelado pelos atores Odilon Wagner e Marcello Airoldi, no dia 25 de novembro, às 20h. A apresentação será realizada no Teatro Maestro Franklin de Carvalho Jr., no bairro Laranjal. A entrada será solidária, mediante a doação de um litro de leite.

Segundo a prefeitura, a troca dos ingressos acontecerá nos dias 23 e 24 de novembro, das 8h às 17h, na Biblioteca Municipal Raul de Leoni, na Vila Santa Cecília. Cada pessoa poderá retirar até dois ingressos por CPF.

Dirigida por Elias Andreato e escrita pelo dramaturgo norte-americano Mark St. Germain, a peça imagina um encontro entre Sigmund Freud, interpretado por Odilon Wagner, e o escritor C.S. Lewis, vivido por Marcello Airoldi.

Ambientada no gabinete de Freud, na Inglaterra, a história apresenta um diálogo entre os dois intelectuais sobre temas como religião, ciência, fé, ateísmo, existência de Deus e sentido da vida.

Com humor e ironia, o espetáculo coloca em discussão diferentes visões de mundo e propõe reflexões sobre a natureza humana, a sexualidade e a morte.

Em cartaz desde 2022, a montagem já ultrapassou 370 apresentações e é baseada no livro “Deus em Questão”, do professor de psiquiatria da Harvard Medical School, Armand M. Nicholi Jr.

articles.title: 'Completely unacceptable': Japan lodges 'very stern protest' after Russian aircraft enter its airspace
articles.summary: Japan scrambled fighter jets after two suspected Russian military aircraft entered its airspace near Okinoshima island in southwestern Fukuoka early
articles.body: Japan scrambled fighter jets after two suspected Russian military aircraft entered its airspace near Okinoshima island in southwestern Fukuoka early Tuesday, and lodged a “very stern protest” with Moscow, the government said.The aircraft entered Japanese airspace shortly after 4 am local time (1900 GMT on Monday), prompting the Air Self-Defence Force (ASDF) to scramble fighter jets and issue warnings, according to top government spokesperson Minoru Kihara.“The violation of our national airspace by Russian aircraft is not only a grave infringement of our country's sovereignty, but also a threat to our security and is completely unacceptable,” Kihara said.“We lodged a very stern protest with Russia through diplomatic channels and strongly demanded measures to prevent any recurrence,” he added.According to Japan's defence ministry, the fighter jets issued warnings and took other unspecified measures towards the suspected Russian aircraft, which continued their flight after entering the country's airspace.Russian aircraft flew towards Pacific after entering Japanese airspaceKihara said the aircraft travelled through the Tsushima Strait before passing between Yonaguni island and Taiwan and heading towards the Pacific Ocean.The incident comes amid heightened regional military activity. South Korea said on Tuesday that it had deployed fighter jets and conducted tactical manoeuvres after several Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone (KADIZ) over the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan.Seoul's Joint Chiefs of Staff said an unspecified number of Russian aircraft entered and later exited the zone in the early hours of Tuesday.However, South Korea clarified that the aircraft had not violated its sovereign airspace.An air defence identification zone is different from a country's sovereign airspace. It is a buffer area where approaching aircraft are identified for security purposes. Military aircraft are generally expected to notify the relevant country before entering such zones, although international law does not make such notification compulsory.The Japan Times reported that foreign military aircraft entering Japanese territorial airspace without permission was extremely unusual. Territorial airspace extends over a country's land and territorial waters, up to 12 nautical miles (around 22 km) from its coastline.Japan-Russia relations deteriorate amid diplomatic disputesThe latest incident comes as relations between Tokyo and Moscow have deteriorated in recent weeks following Russia's arrest of a Japanese journalist on espionage allegations and its seizure of assets belonging to Japan Tobacco in Russia.Japan and Russia also have a decades-old territorial dispute over a group of Pacific islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories and in Russia as the Kuril Islands. The Soviet Union seized the islands in 1945.In August, Japan protested Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit to the disputed islands. It was the first visit by a Russian president to the territory since Dmitry Medvedev's trip in 2010. Tokyo also objected to Russia's announcement of missile tests off one of the islands visited by Putin.Japan had lodged a similar “very serious protest” with Moscow in 2024 after a Russian patrol aircraft entered its airspace three times. That was the first confirmed Russian airspace incursion since 2019, according to news agency AFP.The latest violation also comes ahead of a scheduled trilateral meeting between Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump on Thursday, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China.Tokyo would be closely watching the summit.You use AI every day. articles.title: US bank outage: What caused Chase problems and Zelle payment delays?
articles.summary: A Chase software bug disrupted US banking transactions and delayed some Zelle payments. Here’s what happened.
articles.body:
Thousands of customers across the United States reported problems accessing banking services and making payments after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase disrupted transactions involving other banks.

The problems on Monday affected customers at several major financial institutions, including Wells Fargo and Bank of America, while some users also reported delays with Zelle payments.

So, what caused the US bank outages, which banks were affected, and have services returned to normal?

Thousands of US customers reported problems accessing online banking services after JPMorgan Chase said a software issue caused knock-on effects for transactions involving other banks.

The disruption extended to customers of at least five other banks, who reported issues accessing services and completing transactions.

According to the French news agency AFP, reports on outage-tracking Downdetector peaked at around 2pm Eastern Standard Time (19:00 GMT) before declining later in the day.

“JPMorgan Chase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in an on-premise hardware system – it is not cyber-related,” said Joe Evangelisti, spokesperson for the bank.

Which US banks were affected by the outages?

Customers of several major US banks reported problems on Monday.

These included JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, US Bank, Truist and Capital One.

However, not all the banks reported problems with their own systems.

Chase confirmed experiencing technical problems, while US Bank said its own systems were not directly affected. Capital One and Truist also said their services were operating normally.

JPMorgan Chase said that a software bug in its internal hardware systems had slowed transaction processing and may have delayed transactions involving other banks.

Some customers said they were not able to access accounts and funds, although Chase said customers continued to have access.

The bank stressed that the disruption was not systemic and that other banks may have experienced delays when processing transactions involving Chase.

Chase is the consumer banking division of JPMorgan Chase, which holds the most assets of any US bank. It handles payments involving other financial institutions, meaning a technical problem at Chase can also delay transactions for customers at other banks, even if those banks’ systems are operating normally.

“This is not a systemic issue – other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us,” Evangelisti added.

Zelle is the peer-to-peer third-party payment system that major US banks use to allow customers to send money to friends and family at near-instant speed.

It is owned by Early Warning Services, an Arizona-based company that is itself owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, US Bank and Wells Fargo.

In the US, some customers also reported problems sending and receiving payments through Zelle.

However, Zelle said its network was operating normally.

The company said that customers access Zelle through participating banks and credit unions so technical problems at those institutions can affect the ability to make a payment even if Zelle’s own systems are fully operational.

US Bank said its systems were not directly affected but warned that customers sending or receiving Zelle payments involving other financial institutions could experience delays.

JPMorgan Chase said that transactions were processing normally again following the disruption.

A Chase spokesperson said that shortly after close of business on Monday, at approximately 6:30pm (23:30 GMT), transactions were posting normally, according to NBC News.

However, the restoration of Chase’s transaction processing does not necessarily mean every delayed payment has been completed.

Are the bank outages connected to the Microsoft and FAA disruptions?

There is no confirmed connection between Monday’s outages and the recent Microsoft outage and disruptions impacting the US government’s transport agency, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

The banking problems followed two major incidents in the US last week.

On Thursday, Microsoft experienced a widespread outage that disrupted services including Outlook. A day later, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop following a technical failure affecting air traffic control communications.

The incidents had different reported causes. JPMorgan Chase said its disruption was due to a software bug, while the FAA disruption involved malfunctioning equipment.

However, Jody Westby, CEO of cybersecurity advisory firm Global Cyber Risk, told Al Jazeera that the series of incidents raised questions about the reliability and security of critical infrastructure.

“I think it’s very concerning that everyone’s just jumping to the conclusion it’s a technical issue, it’s a software bug, it was old equipment,” she said.

“I don’t think that any of that is a complete explanation the public deserves.”

Westby said she believed more detailed investigations were needed.

“My concern is that we are not diligently looking into these incidents and analysing them, and even with a global working group to make sure that we can determine whether there are any correlations.”

articles.title: Shakira's foundation began building schools for children in Colombia decades ago; in 2025, it helped deliver seven new schools with the education ministry, benefiting more than 5,000 children each year
articles.summary: Shakira’s Fundación Pies Descalzos has spent decades working to expand access to quality education in Colombia, and its recent school building efforts
articles.body: Shakira’s Fundación Pies Descalzos has spent decades working to expand access to quality education in Colombia, and its recent school building efforts show how far that work has grown. In 2025, the foundation delivered seven new schools alongside Colombia’s Ministry of Education in La Guajira and Tibú, benefiting more than 5,000 children each year, according to the foundation’s own timeline and reporting by Borgen Magazine and TIME.The milestone reflects a commitment that began in 1997, when Shakira created the foundation after her first international success. What started as an effort focused on children affected by displacement and nutrition has evolved into a long running education programme that builds schools, trains teachers, supports families, and works in some of Colombia’s most underserved regions.A foundation built around educationFundación Pies Descalzos, also known as the Barefoot Foundation, was created by Shakira in 1997. Its early work focused on people displaced by violence and on nutrition issues affecting children and adolescents, but education became the centre of its mission.The foundation says its goal is to ensure that no child is left behind. It develops educational infrastructure, improves access to schooling, and works with teachers, families, and local communities to support school retention.Shakira has described education as a path toward change, opportunity, and stronger communities. TIME reported that she has spent nearly 30 years supporting education in Colombia through the foundation, with a focus on regions that have often been neglected.Seven schools in 2025In 2025, the foundation delivered seven new schools in partnership with Colombia’s Ministry of Education. The schools were located in La Guajira and Tibú, two areas where access to quality education has been limited by geography, poverty, and instability.The foundation says the new schools benefit more than 5,000 children and young people each year. The delivery formed part of the Todos al Cole project, an initiative aimed at improving school access and helping children remain in education.The project did not appear overnight. In 2024, the foundation and the ministry had already delivered two new schools in La Guajira, one in Riohacha serving 1,200 students and another in Uribia serving 800.Building beyond classroomsThe foundation’s work goes beyond constructing buildings. Its schools provide meals to students and psychosocial support to children and their families, knowing that learning is more than desks, books and teachers.The organisation also invests in teacher training and community engagement. TIME reported that the foundation has trained more than 12,000 teachers and has built or renovated 19 schools since its inception, reaching more than 224,000 children.These efforts are designed to create lasting change rather than short term relief. By combining infrastructure with educational support and family services, the foundation aims to help children stay in school and build a path toward a better future.A long history of expansionThe foundation’s first school opened in Barranquilla in 2009, serving more than 1,000 students each year. That project marked the beginning of a broader effort to build educational institutions in communities with limited access to quality schooling.In 2014, the foundation opened its first school in Cartagena, in the Lomas del Peyé neighbourhood. The school was designed to serve more than 1,000 students annually and became part of a growing network of Pies Descalzos institutions.By 2021, the foundation’s work had expanded to more than 300 schools across Colombia, reaching more than 224,000 children and young people since 2003. The organisation says its projects now span cities and rural areas, including Barranquilla, Cartagena, Quibdó, Soacha, La Guajira, and Norte de Santander.Why the work mattersColombia’s education challenges are often most severe in regions affected by poverty, conflict, and limited public services. In Chocó, for example, Borgen Magazine reported that most residents live in poverty and that a 2026 earthquake damaged or destroyed hundreds of schools.Shakira has argued that every day a child spends out of school is a day they lose an opportunity to build their future. Her foundation’s response has been to invest in schools, teachers, and community support in places where educational access can be fragile.The 2025 school deliveries show that this approach can produce measurable results. Seven new schools and more than 5,000 children served each year represent a significant expansion of access in areas where a safe, well equipped classroom can make a major difference.Recognition and ongoing workThe foundation’s work has drawn recognition beyond Colombia. TIME included Shakira in its TIME100 Philanthropy 2026 list, noting that the Barefoot Foundation mobilised more resources for education than any other civil society organisation in Colombia between 2021 and 2024.The foundation has also continued to expand its partnerships. In 2025, it worked with ICETEX to support young people from Pies Descalzos schools as they considered paths toward higher education.The organisation’s latest school in Tibú was completed in September, according to TIME. Shakira said the children of Tibú would be able to begin a new chapter in their lives, reflecting the foundation’s belief that education can change not only individual futures but entire communities.A legacy still growingShakira’s foundation began with a simple idea: that children in vulnerable communities deserve access to education. Nearly three decades later, that idea has grown into a network of schools, trained teachers, and support programmes reaching thousands of children each year.The delivery of seven schools to the Ministry of Education in 2025 is a major milestone in that story. It demonstrates how long term commitment can translate into visible change through sustained investment, local partnerships and a focus on underserved regions.The impact is immediate for the children who attend these new schools. For the communities around them, it may shape opportunities for years to come.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Sweden buried geocell grids beneath two forest-road sections near Grums; field tests found load-bearing capacity 52% to 64% higher than on a thicker untreated comparison section
articles.summary: Discover how Sweden's innovative use of geocell grids under forest roads near Grums has significantly increased load-bearing capacity, providing a cost-effective solution to heavy truck challenges and climate change effects.
articles.body: Anyone who has ever driven on a muddy back road after a heavy rain probably knows how quickly a wheel can sink. Forest roads in Sweden face this problem all the time, and the trucks that are allowed on these roads have only become heavier. A February 2025 article from VTI, the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, said tests near Grums found a good fix for the problem. Engineers buried geocell grids under two sections of a forest road. Those sections had 52% to 64% greater load-bearing capacity than the thicker comparison section without geocells.Why Sweden's forest roads are under pressureMost of the forest roads in Sweden were built to older standards. They were built neither for the present-day trucks nor the weather. VTI explains that the maximum legal gross weight of a loaded truck went up from 64 to 74 tonnes. Moreover, climate change has brought heavier rains in short intervals. Roads are damaged and vehicles end up getting trapped. The results are reported by the project named “Solutions for faster development of forest roads.” VTI led the project, which Vinnova funded. It is said to be one of the biggest research projects conducted by the Swedish forest industry. There were 11 partners in this research project, among whom were some big names in the forest industry. Five options for road reinforcement were tested; geocells were one of them.How the geocell worked VTI describes a geocell as a grid placed in the road and filled with gravel. The cells keep the stones in place and help the road carry weight. The trial was conducted by the forestry company Stora Enso. According to a 2026 paper, ‘Performance evaluation of geocell-reinforced gravel road on waterlogged ground,’ published in European Transport Studies, three full-scale test sections were built on waterlogged ground. Two of them used geocells, one filled with crushed rock, and one filled with local material. The third was a normal road, without geocells. It was nearly twice as thick, so it was difficult to beat.What the measurements showedA lightweight deflectometer was used in this case. It is a machine that drops a weight on the surface of the road and monitors how the ground responds. Vehicles were driven over the sections first. After that, the two geocell sections showed 52% to 64% greater bearing capacity than the comparison section, the paper reports. VTI adds that this even held though the soil had a relatively high moisture content. Dina Kuttah, the project manager and senior researcher at VTI, said the results were much clearer and more positive than she had expected. Moreover, she did not expect some of the solutions to prove so cost-effective. Overall, most of the solutions worked well, but VTI described geocells as giving the biggest improvement. However, it's also worth noting that the comparison involved a single, thicker reference section. The institute also rated them as the most economical choice for strength per metre of road gained.Cost, local stone and some cautions A strong road is only useful to people if they can afford to build it. Costs have been reviewed in a VTI report, ‘Lösningar för snabbare utveckling av skogsbilvägar i Sverige.’ It found Stora Enso’s two geocell roads to be the most cost-effective in the project. The reference section had lower bearing capacity and higher construction cost. The report also says this was the first time in Sweden's forest industry that a gravel road was built on waterlogged soil. Local fill, the researchers note, performed as well as or even better than imported crushed rock. It could cut transport costs and even reduce damage done to nature. A little caution is still needed. One co-author works for Stora Enso, the company that ran the trial. The tests were also just on three sections in Sweden, so other soils and climates could give different results.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1941, airman Daniel Clifford recorded a radio greeting while training in Canada; killed before meeting his baby daughter, she heard his voice for the first time more than 80 years later
articles.summary: In a heartwarming reunion, Margaret hears her late father's voice for the first time through a 1941 radio recording, 80 years after he went missing in action during WWII.
articles.body: Think about the last voice note you sent to your friend. It might have taken only a few seconds and is probably still on your phone. Now imagine a voice message that waited more than 80 years just to be heard. Margaret, in her 80s, heard her father's voice for the first time in 2024. He was Daniel Clifford, a New Zealand airman. He went missing in action in January 1942, less than six months after Margaret’s birth. According to the Auckland War Memorial Museum, a sound researcher had located his wartime recording and used its Online Cenotaph database to reach his family.A clerk who wanted to fly Daniel grew up in Helensville, north of Auckland, where he worked as a clerk for New Zealand Railways. He applied for aircrew training in October 1939, not long after the Second World War broke out. He spent a year training in New Zealand. Before leaving to go to Canada in December 1940, he married his fiancée, Jean Wemyss. She was pregnant when he left. These details are provided in a narrative written by sound researcher Sarah Johnston, published by Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision, the audiovisual archive of New Zealand. In Canada, he trained as an air observer, a kind of navigator under the Empire Air Training Scheme, which trained over 8,000 New Zealanders.A message recorded far away from home During their time there, Daniel and five other airmen recorded messages to send home. Johnston says the disc was probably made in early 1941 at a radio station in London, Ontario, most likely the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation. The disc is thought to have travelled from Canada to New Zealand to Egypt and then back to New Zealand. Discs were not common at the time. So it was possible that it was sent to Egypt, where broadcasters used its blank side in May 1941. The Canadian side of the disc was marked “Defective”, which may mean it never aired.A loss that came too soon Daniel was commissioned as a pilot officer after training in Canada. In July 1941, he served with No. 142 Squadron at Binbrook, Lincolnshire, England. Just one month later, on 4 August 1941, his daughter Margaret was born on the other side of the globe. In late 1941, Jean had sent him a picture of the baby, and the family knew he had received it. On 18 January 1942, his bomber was lost on a mission to Bremen, Germany. They never found his body. He was only 23 years old when he died. Service in Bomber Command was particularly dangerous, with a casualty rate exceeding 50%. He is named on the Runnymede Memorial in Britain, which commemorates airmen with no known graves.How a stranger found his family In 2024, Johnston was researching wartime recordings made by New Zealand broadcasters when she found the disc. The Canadian side didn't have a label, so she identified the speakers by listening carefully and checking names on Online Cenotaph. The database helped make the link. Daniel's granddaughter, Rochelle Cook, added a contribution to his page and left her email in 2016. Johnston emailed her and sent the audio file. Rochelle played it for her mother, Margaret. Margaret recognised the place names in the greeting as the homes of relatives and friends and heard her father’s voice at last. Rochelle said that hearing it was very moving and that it had a deep impact on Margaret and the wider family.Daniel’s message made trips around the world on a single disc and took over 80 years to reach his daughter. The Auckland Museum says stories like this show what digital archives can do as families add photos, documents and memories to its records. Daniel never got to meet Margaret, but she had now finally heard the message he left 80 years back.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2012, California professor Yaser Abu-Mostafa opened Caltech’s full machine-learning class online for free; its lectures have drawn more than 8 million views
articles.summary: Explore the groundbreaking free machine learning course offered by Caltech professor Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa, attracting over 9 million views and providing learners worldwide with full access to the curriculum.
articles.body: In 2012, Caltech professor Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa made his complete machine-learning course available online for free, giving people around the world access to the same class at the California Institute of Technology. The course, named Learning From Data: Introductory Machine Learning Course, was Caltech’s first-ever live broadcast of a full course. The lectures of this course have received more than 9 million views on YouTube and other servers, as mentioned on the official course site. According to the course page on Caltech’s website, the course was built from recordings of the lectures broadcast live in April and May 2012. According to the course page, the course has 18 lectures of about 60 minutes each, plus Q&A sessions that let online viewers take part. The content is organized as a topic-by-topic video library for self-learners.Caltech broadcast its first complete course online in 2012Caltech announced the course in a March 30, 2012 news release, with the live lectures starting on April 3. Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa, a professor of electrical engineering and computer science at Caltech, delivered them as part of his usual teaching. The online course was meant to serve learners who could not be present at the Caltech campus to attend the class there. The material and the level of teaching stayed the same as in the on-campus course. What changed was the delivery: Abu-Mostafa adapted the class for online viewers, including live Q&A with the online audience. In an interview conducted on September 21, 2012, with Caltech’s ENGenious, he stated that the availability of the entire course was an opportunity for people to take a Caltech class. Lectures were provided through iTunes U, YouTube and Caltech’s server. According to the interview in Caltech’s ENGenious magazine, the course had more than 60,000 subscribers on iTunes U alone.The 18 lectures covered key machine-learning conceptsLearning From Data introduced the students to both theory and practice of machine learning. The course page lists topics such as linear models, neural networks, support vector machines, regularisation, validation and kernel methods. Among other issues were such notions as overfitting, sampling bias and Data snooping. This enabled the students to understand how the machine-learning systems learn from examples and how their performance is evaluated.One can also comprehend why the system, which operates perfectly on training data, can fail when encountering new data. The course page lists eight homework sets and a final exam and it asks students to know basic probability, matrices and calculus beforehand. The knowledge of probability, matrices and calculus was supposed to be acquired by the students prior to watching the classes. This made the web course more than just a set of introductory videos. The learners were able to go through the lessons and do the corresponding homework and assignments and the Q&A sessions gave the viewers an opportunity to participate in the process of learning during the lecture.The course continues to reach learners onlineAccording to the official website of the course, there are currently more than 9 million views on YouTube and other servers. The 9 million views represent views of videos and not individual students who have taken the course. The virtual library lets learners access individual topics on their own schedule. They get an opportunity to go back and forth and learn from the available course materials. The idea of Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa broadcasting the whole class ensured that learners who were not at Caltech could access the class taught at the Institute. The fact that the class is still accessible ensures that learners will continue accessing it even many years down the line. It was originally a classroom broadcast that was added in 2012. It has since grown into an online educational platform for those interested in understanding machine learning.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Turkey raids another opposition tv channel, appoints trustees to take over operations
articles.summary: Turkish authorities on Tuesday raided the headquarters of Sozcu TV, one of the country's prominent opposition-aligned television networks, detaining
articles.body: Turkish authorities on Tuesday raided the headquarters of Sozcu TV, one of the country's prominent opposition-aligned television networks, detaining several executives and appointing trustees to oversee its operations. The action has drawn criticism from media freedom advocates, who view it as another move in an expanding crackdown on independent journalism.According to the news agency AP, the raid, which took place before dawn, comes just weeks after trustees were appointed to take control of another opposition-leaning broadcaster, Halk TV, as part of a corruption investigation. Critics have questioned the motives behind the action, alleging that it was politically driven.Media freedom in Turkey has faced growing restrictions during the more than two decades of president Recep Tayyip Erdogan's rule. A large proportion of the country's media outlets are either controlled by the government or aligned with it. Turkey ranks 163rd among 180 countries in the Reporters Without Borders' World Press Freedom Index.According to a statement from the Istanbul chief public prosecutor's Office, the action against Sozcu TV is linked to an investigation into alleged violations of Turkey's laws on terrorist financing and suspected connections with a network led by US-based cleric Fethullah Gulen.Gulen, who died in 2024, was accused by the Turkish government of masterminding the failed military coup in 2016. Authorities subsequently designated his network of supporters as a terrorist organisation, although the cleric denied the allegations.Prosecutors said they suspected that Sozcu TV and other media organisations associated with its owner, Burak Akbay, had received funding through overseas accounts.Ozgur Ozel, leader of the main opposition new party, condemned the raid and accused Erdogan's government of being unwilling to tolerate criticism or uncomfortable truths.He also vowed that the opposition would not "surrender to these would-be dictators".Meanwhile, Sozcu TV's regular early morning news programme was replaced on Tuesday by a pre-recorded discussion focusing on longevity, following the raid and the detention of its executives.You use AI every day. articles.body: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans have another reason to get excited as two of the biggest internet streamers, Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed, have announced plans to play the highly awaited game live on November 18. However, their chosen streaming times have caught everyone's attention. Both streamers plan to go live hours before GTA 6 officially launches in the US. Their announcements have also raised questions about whether they have found a way to access the game early or will stream from a region where it becomes available sooner.Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed announce GTA 6 livestreams before US launchKai Cenat shared his plans through an Instagram post, revealing that he will stream the full GTA 6 playthrough on November 18 at 8 PM ET. His Instagram announcement carried a simple but exciting message: "GTA 6 FULL PLAY THROUGH."This means Kai is not planning to play just a small part of the game. He wants to complete the entire experience live in front of his viewers. He has also spent time getting ready for this moment. Between November 5 and November 11, Kai played the five main GTA games that came before GTA 6. These included GTA III, Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV and GTA V. He spent more than 130 hours playing them live.IShowSpeed also announced his GTA 6 livestream through Instagram. His post said, "LIVE PLAYING GTA 6 NOV 18 AT 9PM." This means Speed plans to start his stream just one hour after Kai.However, there is an important detail behind these announcements. GTA 6 is set to launch in the US at midnight ET on November 19. This means Kai's stream is planned four hours before the US launch, while Speed's stream is planned three hours before it.How will the streamers play GTA 6 before its official US release?The timing of both announcements has raised an interesting question. How will Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed play GTA 6 before it officially launches in the US?Rockstar Games is using a local midnight release system for GTA 6. This means the game will become available at midnight on November 19 in different regions around the world. As a result, some countries will get access to the game before players in the US.For example, GTA 6 will become available in London at 7 PM ET on November 18. This is one hour before Kai's planned stream and two hours before Speed's stream. This has led to questions about whether either streamer will play from a region where the game is already available.However, neither streamer has confirmed that they have early access or explained how they plan to start playing before the US release.With two major creators announcing streams on the same night, GTA 6 is already set for a huge streaming event. articles.title: At eight, Abigail Watt built three AI apps, including a 3D explorer and a children’s book community, then taught all 30 classmates to use AI creatively; she was the youngest finalist at the 2026 Overt STEM Awards
articles.summary: At eight, most children are still figuring out how to use technology for schoolwork and entertainment.
articles.body: At eight, most children are still figuring out how to use technology for schoolwork and entertainment. Abigail Watt, however, has already begun creating things with it. The young student has developed three artificial intelligence applications, including a 3D explorer and an online book community for children, and taken her interest a step further by teaching all 30 of her classmates how to use AI creatively. Her work has now earned her recognition at the 2026 Overt STEM Awards in Milton Keynes, where she became the youngest finalist and winner in the school's category.As per a report by Business MK, Abigail won the Future Force in STEM award in the school-age category at the ceremony held at Unity Place on November 3. Her projects stood out among entries from a field of more than 50 finalists, which included young innovators, researchers, educators and established organisations working across science, technology, engineering and mathematics.Abigail's three applications are a 3D Explorer Map, an Art App and Page Pals, an online book community designed specifically for children. While the names offer a glimpse into the range of her interests, the projects also demonstrate how she is exploring different ways of using AI, from interactive exploration and creativity to encouraging children to engage with books. The third project, Page Pals, is particularly interesting because it brings technology into the world of children's reading. Rather than treating AI only as a tool for completing tasks, the idea of a book community gives young readers a digital space centred on their interest in stories and books.Her other projects reflect a similar willingness to experiment. The 3D Explorer Map points towards an interest in interactive digital experiences, while the Art App explores the creative possibilities of technology. Together, the three applications earned her recognition from the Overt STEM Awards, which celebrate contributions to science, technology, engineering and mathematics across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor.Her school, Caroline Haslett Primary School, announced the achievement on November 6, describing Abigail, identified in its announcement as Abigail W (Joules), as the youngest finalist and winner in the awards' history. The school said she had impressed the judges with her three applications and her dedication to sharing AI knowledge with her classmates. It also noted that she faced competition from older finalists, including an A-level student presenting medical devices and AI research.The recognition places Abigail among a wider group of people and organisations whose work was celebrated at this year's awards. The event brought together more than 50 finalists from across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor, a region spanning areas between Oxford and Cambridge that has become an important centre for research, education, technology and innovation.The awards covered a broad range of achievements. At the University of Buckingham, Jean D'Amour Kwizera received the AI Impact award for developing a system that uses smartphone images, computer vision, object detection and machine learning to help identify counterfeit medicines. Nathan Luccarini of The Bedford College Group won the Future Force in STEM award in the further and higher education category for developing an esports qualification and digital learning pathways. His colleague Duncan Laughton was recognised for moving from engineering into teaching and helping learners build confidence in mathematics.Other winners included STEM On Track, an educational programme that uses go-kart design and racing to introduce students to engineering, physics and teamwork. It received both the STEM Enrichment Initiative award and the overall STEM Champion title. The programme has reached more than 2,400 students across over 140 school teams.The awards also recognised people working to make STEM careers more accessible. Natalie Desty, founder of STEM Returners, received the Women in STEM Champion award, while Pearl Oguchi, founder of the Black Women in Tech community, received the Lifetime Impact in STEM award for her 22-year contribution to technology.The Overt STEM Awards were organised by Events Together and expanded the reach of the earlier MK STEM Awards to recognise talent across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor. Its categories span school-age projects, higher education, research, industry innovation, mentoring and inclusion. The Future Force in STEM school-age category is intended to showcase young learners between five and 18 who are making an impact through STEM projects.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Reba McEntire opened her personal archive for a 255-lot Nashville charity auction in October, offering five decades of stage gowns, jewellery and keepsakes to support the Reba McEntire Fund and its nonprofit work
articles.summary: A dress worn on a country music awards stage, a rhinestone-covered suit from a television singing competition and scripts marked with handwritten notes
articles.body: A dress worn on a country music awards stage, a rhinestone-covered suit from a television singing competition and scripts marked with handwritten notes from a sitcom career spanning six years, these were among the personal keepsakes Reba McEntire put up for auction as she opened a window into five decades of her life in entertainment. The country music star's collection went under the hammer in Nashville on October 23, with 255 lots offered through Julien’s Auctions to benefit the Reba McEntire Fund and its nonprofit initiatives across the US.Titled 'The Reba Collection', the benefit auction was held at the Musicians Hall of Fame & Museum at the Historic Nashville Municipal Auditorium. The collection brought together pieces from McEntire's wardrobe, jewellery box and professional archive, including stage and screen-worn gowns, boots, belt buckles, awards, jewellery and personal memorabilia. According to the auction announcement on McEntire's official website, all proceeds were designated to support the fund.For McEntire, the sale was an opportunity to let fans take home something more personal than conventional merchandise. The singer said her team had carefully looked after the clothes over the years, but she felt it was time for them to move on and find new homes. She added that buyers would have both the outfit and the story behind it, knowing that she had worn the piece herself.The collection offered a timeline of a career that moved between country music stages, television studios and film sets. McEntire, who has sold more than 58 million albums worldwide and recorded 35 career No. 1 singles, has spent more than five decades building a presence across entertainment. A member of the Country Music Hall of Fame and a recipient of the 2018 Kennedy Center Honors, she has also starred in her own sitcom and appeared as a coach on NBC's 'The Voice'.Some of the most recognisable pieces in the auction came from her appearances at major country music events. Among them was a forest-green silk gown with leather-studded trim that McEntire wore at the 2009 Academy of Country Music Awards in Las Vegas. The ceremony was significant for another reason: it marked her 11th time hosting the awards. The gown was offered with a signed photograph. Another highlight was a silver tinsel Roberto Cavalli dress and matching heels worn at the 1987 Academy of Country Music Awards and later for Bob Hope's television Christmas special. The outfit reflected the theatrical side of McEntire's stage image, which became known for its elaborate silhouettes, embellishments and frequent changes during performances.The catalogue also reached into her television career. Three personal final-draft scripts from her sitcom 'Reba', which ran from 2001 to 2007, were included in the sale. The scripts were signed and carried handwritten annotations throughout, offering a glimpse of the preparation behind the show. One was labelled as her study script for a Tuesday recording, with changes noted up to 1.50 pm. Two scripts from NBC's 'Happy's Place', which premiered in 2024, were also part of the collection.Her more recent television appearances were represented by a rhinestone-covered hot-pink suit worn on 'The Voice' in 2023. Other items included her signature boots and belt buckles, awards and a Franck Muller 18-karat rose-gold watch set with diamonds. The auction catalogue also featured a personalised bronze belt buckle bearing her name, accompanied by its original signed box.For fans, the appeal lay in the opportunity to own an object connected to a particular moment in her career. For the singer, the sale also meant that items carefully preserved by her team could continue to be appreciated rather than remain in storage. The charitable beneficiary was central to the event. The Reba McEntire Fund was created by the singer to support projects across the United States. Its stated priorities include improving the health and well-being of families, recognising and supporting those who have served, and creating opportunities for young people. The auction announcement said the sale was intended to generate both financial support and awareness for local and national nonprofit initiatives.The fund's three areas of focus reflect causes that extend beyond the music industry. Family well-being, support for veterans and opportunities for young people are the broad themes through which it backs charitable work. By directing the auction proceeds towards the fund, McEntire connected objects from her own professional journey with initiatives intended to benefit communities.Julien’s Auctions co-founder and executive director Martin Nolan said the collection offered fans a personal connection to the memories and milestones that shaped McEntire's career. The auction house described the sale as a celebration of five decades of fashion and entertainment, bringing together material from her work in music, television and film.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Pope Leo on Tuesday said he was not planning to change the Catholic Church's position on allowing married men to become priests, but did not rule out the
articles.body: Pope Leo on Tuesday said he was not planning to change the Catholic Church's position on allowing married men to become priests, but did not rule out the possibility of a shift in the future. He described the issue as "complicated" and "divisive", saying his priority was to maintain unity within the 1.4-billion-member Church."I'm very well aware many people are not in agreement with that approach. articles.body: A Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on November 16, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said, adding that all crew members were safe and no injuries had been reported.In a statement, Sonowal said the vessel, named TARA GAS, had a total crew of 25, including 24 Indian nationals, and that all of them were safe."On Nov 16, Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS, carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz. We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and well-being of our seafarers," he said in a post on X.The incident comes amid heightened maritime security concerns in and around the Strait of Hormuz, with at least four oil tankers reportedly damaged over the past 24 hours.The Iranian Navy said a fourth tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. It alleged that the vessel was navigating through a restricted maritime zone with its navigation systems switched off.In a statement carried by Iranian state broadcaster Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), the Navy's Public Relations department said the tanker had been travelling in a restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz with its navigation systems turned off.The Iranian Navy also warned shipping operators against entering restricted maritime areas without coordinating with the country's armed forces."The result of any illegal movement, without coordination with the armed forces, and against regulations, is encountering mines and fires," the statement said, as reported by Al Jazeera.Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency reported an attack on a tanker seven nautical miles off Khasab in Oman. Spokesperson Lauren Bis said the administration was monitoring potential threats but added that “at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland”.During Tuesday's interaction, Trump was also asked whether he would seek help from Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin to bring the conflict to an end. articles.title: An Indiana mother sought to change custody of her three children and access their father's mental-health records; an appeals court rejected her bid, upheld $18,500 in legal fees and ordered her to pay more
articles.summary: An Indiana mother who tried to regain sole legal custody of her three children from her former husband and gain access to his mental-health records has
articles.body: An Indiana mother who tried to regain sole legal custody of her three children from her former husband and gain access to his mental-health records has lost her appeal. She must also pay more of his legal costs. In a ruling issued on 16 November 2026, the Indiana Court of Appeals rejected all the challenges brought by Sember Darland-Chappell against her former husband, Andrew Hahn. A three-judge panel upheld a Hamilton Superior Court order that denied her request to change custody, refused to let her see Hahn's therapy notes and ordered her to pay $18,500 towards his trial lawyer's fees. The appeals court also approved Hahn's request for appellate legal fees and sent the case back to the trial court to decide how much more she must pay. Judge Cale Bradford wrote the decision. Judges Patricia Riley Bailey and Elaine Brown Altice agreed with the ruling.Seven years of court battlesDarland-Chappell and Hahn divorced on 19 February 2020, according to the Indiana Court of Appeals decision. Under their original divorce order, the former couple shared legal custody of their three children, who were born in October 2009, June 2011 and October 2013. However, Darland-Chappell had primary physical custody. Hahn had regular parenting time with the children on Wednesday evenings and every other weekend. The dispute grew in June 2021 when Hahn asked the court to change legal custody and parenting time. Darland-Chappell filed a request of her own and asked the court to arrange a formal child custody evaluation. Clinical psychologist Dr Bart Ferraro carried out the evaluation between February and May 2022. He prepared a 131-page report.The trial court relied heavily on Dr Ferraro's recommendations. On 16 May 2023, it gave Hahn sole legal custody and changed the physical parenting schedule so that the children would spend alternating full weeks with each parent. Darland-Chappell filed a request to regain custody in November 2023. The trial court rejected it in May 2024 after holding a three-day hearing. On 2 January 2025, she filed another request to change custody, along with a motion asking for a different judge. In her filing, Darland-Chappell claimed Hahn "has weaponized his sole legal custody status and has seemed to be more focused on lording that over [Mother], rather than on making sound decisions for the [C]hildren." She also argued that alternating weeks with each parent "provides no consistency or continuity for the [C]hildren."Fight over therapy records and guardian ad litemAfter a new judge took over the case, Darland-Chappell filed several requests before the custody hearing. In late January 2025, she asked the court to appoint a guardian ad litem, an independent person who looks after children's interests in court cases. She argued that a new evaluation was needed because Dr Ferraro's report was almost three years old. Hahn opposed the request. He pointed out that the children had been regularly seeing a therapist since 2020. The trial court rejected her request in March 2025. Darland-Chappell also asked the judge to speak privately with all three children. She also issued a subpoena for records held by Vanessa McCaskey, the family therapist who worked with Hahn and the children. When McCaskey asked the court to cancel the subpoena, Darland-Chappell filed a request in July 2025 to force the release of Hahn's mental-health records under Indiana Code section 16-39-3-3.Both Hahn and McCaskey told the court that releasing the records could harm the therapy process. McCaskey said Hahn might stop speaking openly during sessions if he thought his words could be given to his former wife. She warned that this could damage the work he was doing to improve his relationship with the children. Hahn also told the court that Darland-Chappell's earlier involvement with another family therapist, Angela Hardy, had seriously disrupted counselling. The children's individual therapist, Dr Natasha Anderson, had then recommended finding a new therapist.On 8 September 2025, the trial court rejected Darland-Chappell's request for Hahn's records. The judge decided that the possible harm to Hahn as a patient was greater than the need to share the records. The judge explained that court-ordered counselling was meant to help the children adjust and improve their relationship with their father. This followed an earlier warning from the court that therapy was not ordered "to give either party the opportunity to reload their quivers with arrows to sling at the other party in the next hearing."Trial court findings and appellate rulingShortly before the main hearing started, Darland-Chappell filed another request on 20 October 2025. She wanted to change the summer parenting schedule. She claimed that she had less freedom than Hahn to plan quality time with the children, partly because of their travel baseball commitments. The Hamilton Superior Court held hearings over three days in October and December 2025. After hearing the evidence, it rejected all of Darland-Chappell's requests and refused to interview the children privately.In its written decision, the trial court found that there had been no major and ongoing change in circumstances since May 2024 that would justify changing custody or the summer schedule. The judge said that approving Darland-Chappell's request "would legalize and institutionalize the very behaviors exhibited by Mother — alienating the [C]hildren from Father and minimizing his role in their lives — which Dr. Ferraro warned the Court against in his extensive [CCE]." The court also said Darland-Chappell had shown little willingness to change her behaviour. The judge believed that making changes would help the children by bringing an end to "the constant onslaught of litigation that has occurred for the past [seven] years."Along with rejecting her custody requests, the trial court ordered Darland-Chappell to pay $18,500 towards Hahn's legal costs. Darland-Chappell appealed the decision. She argued that the trial court had made several mistakes by refusing to appoint a guardian ad litem, declining to speak privately with the children, blocking access to Hahn's therapy records, rejecting her request to change custody and ordering her to pay $18,500 in legal fees. The Indiana Court of Appeals rejected all her arguments. It found that the trial court had acted within its legal powers and had based its decisions on the extensive evidence and earlier clinical evaluations. The appeals court also ruled in Hahn's favour on his request for appellate attorney fees. The case will now return to Hamilton Superior Court, where the judge will work out the additional amount Darland-Chappell must pay for Hahn's legal costs during the appeal.You use AI every day.
